verdict: accepted and promoted (default path, rollback lever HIPENGINE_GEMMA4_MOE_DOWN_MMQ)
recorded: 2026-09-28, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Gemma 4 26B-A4B, UD-Q4_K_XL, 2048-token prefill
why: the expert route is 43.4% of gfx1151 prefill and had no measured mechanism. It now does, and the mechanism names a specific kernel that already exists and is already wired for another model in this tree. This row exists so the next unit starts from the measurement instead of re-deriving it.
command: env -u HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/gemma4_prefill_route_ablation.py --prompt 2048 --repeats 2
method: The ablation's no_experts arm times the prefill with the expert launches skipped. A separate probe wraps gemma4_project_experts_gate_up_mmq, gemma4_project_experts_rows and gemma4_project_experts_grouped_prefill and times each real launch with HIP events during a 2048-token Gemma4Runner.forward. Note the wrappers nest: gemma4_project_experts_rows is the outer entry point and calls gemma4_project_experts_grouped_prefill, so the rows row contains the grouped row and the difference is the selected-GEMV fallback.

baseline.note: measured with the prefill attention weight-reuse change already landed

route_shares.dense_q8_0: unmeasured - the no_dense_q8 and no_all_gemv arms both save about -1%, which cannot be right

expert_breakdown_measured.method: HIP events around each real launch, 2048-token prefill
expert_breakdown_measured.note: gate_up_mmq is the gate/up projection (120 launches, 4 chunks x 30 layers). The down projection is the rows/grouped_prefill pair. The 659.54 ms difference between rows and grouped_prefill is the selected-GEMV fallback for the rows the grouped route does not take.

finding.statement: the down projection is about 12x slower per FLOP than the gate/up projection on the same layer, and the difference is the quantization route, not the shape

geometry.ffn_gate_up_exps: shape (128, 1408, 2816), Q4_K - fused gate+up, so hidden 2816 -> 2 x 704
geometry.ffn_down_exps: shape (128, 2816, 704), Q5_1 - down, so intermediate 704 -> hidden 2816

finding.root_cause: Q5_1 has no MMQ route in the gemma4 expert dispatch. gemma4_project_experts_gate_up_mmq returns False for any quant_key other than gguf_q4_k and gguf_q5_k, so the Q5_1 down projection falls to the fp32 grouped family, whose best variant runs at 8.6 GB/s where the Q4_K MMQ runs at 67 GB/s.
finding.the_family_is_already_tuned: the winning variant is selected_grouped_prefill_staged_out4_bf16_bf16_out (116 of 120 launches; the other 4 are the Q5_K and Q8_0 layers). Its own docstring records it as the measured optimum of a small sweep, 1.91x over the incumbent at the Gemma 4 down projection. So this is not an untuned kernel; it is a route that lacks an MMQ path.
finding.why_it_is_not_bandwidth_bound: the staged kernel reads each weight exactly once - it stages d, m and qh per (output column, k-chunk) into shared memory and the grid is (out_features/OUT_TILE, num_experts) with OUT_TILE 4. 174.4 MB per launch at 20.97 ms is 8.6 GB/s, 3.4% of the 256 GB/s this host reaches on a pack8 Q8_0 GEMV. Neither the bytes nor the instruction count explain the time.
finding.shape_of_the_kernel: launch_q5_1_staged_grouped uses out_tile 4, ROW_BATCH 4, K_TILE 256, 128 threads, grid (704, 128) = 90112 blocks. Each block computes 4 output columns x 4 rows and runs a 7-level barrier tree per row batch, so 8 barriers per row batch and about 64 per block. Each expert has about 32 rows at this geometry, so 8 row batches.

named_implementation_path.it_is_already_wired_for_another_model: hipengine/runtime/qwen4_exp_runner.py lines 4170-4210 run it behind HIPENGINE_QWEN4_EXP_Q5_1_MMQ_PREFILL for Qwen4-Exp's expert_down when the weight is Q5_1. The activation pack it needs is gguf_q8_1_mmq_ds4_pack_bf16, the same DS4 Q8_1 pack the gemma4 Q4_K gate_up MMQ route already calls.
named_implementation_path.it_is_not_reachable_from_gemma4: gemma4_project_experts_grouped_prefill iterates _GROUPED_PREFILL_VARIANTS, which does not contain q5_1_mmq_ds4_selected_prefill_bf16_bf16_out, and the MMQ entry point takes x_ds4 rather than raw bf16 so it cannot be added to that tuple. Reaching it needs an explicit route in gemma4_experts.py: pack the down input with gguf_q8_1_mmq_ds4_pack_bf16, then call the MMQ kernel.
named_implementation_path.scratch_is_already_big_enough: Gemma4ExpertScratch sizes mmq_workspace at lanes * (hidden_size // 128) * 144 * _MMQ_ACTIVATION_PASSES = 12976128 bytes at 4096 lanes. The down projection needs lanes * ceil(intermediate/128) * 144 = 4096 * 6 * 144 = 3538944 bytes. It fits with room to spare, so no new buffer is required.

the_blocker.constraint: the Q5_1 MMQ kernel requires in_features % 128 == 0. This artifact's down width is 704, and 704 % 128 = 64.
the_blocker.it_is_a_real_constraint_not_a_soft_guard: the kernel computes ds4_blocks = in_features / Q8_1_MMQ_BLOCK (integer division, so 5 for 704) and each kb consumes 4 Q5_1 blocks = 128 weight elements. 5 x 128 = 640, so it would silently drop the last 64 elements. The guard at line 183 exists to prevent exactly that, not to be conservative.
the_blocker.the_fix_is_bounded: handle a partial trailing group: loop ds4_blocks over ceil(in_features/128) and, when (kb+1)*128 > in_features, read only the Q5_1 blocks that exist and zero the rest rather than reading 48 bytes past the row end. The activation pack must write a half-filled trailing DS4 block the same way. Both sides are a few lines, not a new kernel.
the_blocker.not_the_only_option: materializing a 768-wide padded copy of ffn_down_exps would also work and needs no kernel change, at the cost of about 174 MB of extra device memory and a load-time pass.

named_implementation_path.arithmetic_note: the MMQ route quantizes the block's activations to DS4 Q8_1, so its arithmetic differs from the fp32 grouped route. It therefore needs the docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md gate for whatever profile it lands on and the docs/OPTIMIZATION.md correctness gates, not the bit-exact argument the attention change used. tests/test_unit_gemma4_expert_route.py already measures the Q4_K MMQ route against its strict owner and is the shape that measurement should take.

expected_effect.if_the_down_reaches_the_q4_k_mmq_rate: 3.1 s -> about 0.4 s, saving about 2.7 s of the 7.191 s prefill, so about 284.8 -> 450 tok/s
expected_effect.against_the_target: llama.cpp pp512 on this host is 1012.98 tok/s, so this closes about 40% of the remaining prefill gap on its own
expected_effect.not_a_promise: the Q5_1 MMQ's rate at this shape has not been measured. The 7.66 TFLOP/s figure is the Q4_K gate_up route at its own shape, and the Q5_1 route's wider weight rows make its reuse pattern different. This is an estimate with a stated basis, not a measured claim.

caveats: The 43.4% expert share is from the ablation's no_experts arm, which skips the launches and therefore produces wrong output. It is a diagnostic and only its timing is read.
The probe's route rows nest, so gate_up_mmq + rows is the expert total and rows already contains grouped_prefill. Adding all five rows double-counts.

The dense Q8_0 share of prefill remains unmeasured. The no_dense_q8 and no_all_gemv arms both report about -1%, which is impossible because skipping every GEMV cannot save less than skipping the experts alone at 43.4%. The arms hook funnels the prefill leaves do not use.
The 11.8x per-FLOP ratio compares two different quantizations at two different shapes. The per-byte ratio of 7.8x is the cleaner comparison and it is the one the root cause rests on.

CORRECTED 2026-09-28: an earlier revision of this artifact claimed the model generates degenerate text. That was wrong. `LLM.generate("The capital of France is")` is a raw-completion call, so the instruction-tuned model is handed a prompt it was never trained on and degenerates -- expected behaviour, not a defect. Through the surface a user reaches, `hipengine serve` with /v1/chat/completions returns 'Paris' for 'What is the capital of France? Answer in one word.' The engine's own render_gemma4_chat renders the artifact's template, and feeding that rendering to Gemma4Runner.forward gives 'The capital of France is Paris.' See worklog/entries/20260928T001500.000000Z-lhl-gemma4-generation-path-correction-*.md.
next: Extend the Q5_1 MMQ kernel and its DS4 activation pack to a partial trailing group, then wire gemma4's down projection to it with an explicit route in gemma4_experts.py. That is the largest single lever left in gfx1151 prefill: about 43% of the step, behind a named kernel that already exists and already runs for another model in this tree.

executed.what_landed: the Q5_1 DS4 DP4A MMQ route is now reachable from gemma4's expert down projection
executed.kernel_change: the Q5_1 MMQ consumer and the DS4 Q8_1 activation pack both handle a partial trailing 128-wide block. The consumer rounds ds4_blocks up and skips the Q5_1 sub-blocks a trailing group does not have; the pack rounds blocks_per_row up and reads 0.0 past `hidden`.
executed.why_padding_is_transparent: the elements past `hidden` are zero, and a zero cannot raise a max_abs or move a sum, so the scale the real elements get is the one they would have got without the padding. The consumer's skipped sub-blocks multiply activation elements that do not exist, so their contribution is zero either way.
executed.route_change: gemma4_project_experts_down_mmq in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_experts.py, tried before the grouped family at the down call site in gemma4_experts_forward_bf16. Gemma4ExpertScratch now sizes mmq_workspace for max(hidden_size, intermediate) so the down's own width cannot overflow the gate_up's buffer.

measured_effect.route_counts: down_mmq32 116 of 120 launches; the grouped family fell from 120 to 4 (the Q5_K and Q8_0 layers)

correctness.kernel_at_the_real_geometry: 4096 compact rows, 128 experts, 704 -> 2816, one plane, against the fp32 grouped owner and against an exact dequant oracle: grouped vs oracle max 0.00789 / mean 0.000712 relative; MMQ vs oracle max 0.01297 / mean 0.001336; MMQ vs grouped max 0.01218 / mean 0.001110. That is the same envelope the Q4_K gate_up MMQ route already runs at.
correctness.model_level: 24 greedy steps from a 300-token prompt, route on vs route off: identical token ids [236795, 568, 609, 568, 609, ...], logits differing by 0.1-0.4 absolute with an unchanged argmax.
correctness.suite: 406 gemma4 tests: 405 passed, 1 failed. The failure is tests/test_unit_gemma4_runner.py::test_incremental_decode_matches_a_dense_prefill and it reports the identical max abs diff 4.417 with and without this change.
correctness.unit_test: tests/test_gpu_gguf_q5_1_mmq_selected_prefill.py is now parametrized over in_features 640 (multiple of 128, the control) and 704 (the artifact's width). Both pass; 704 raised ValueError before this change.

executed.execution_profile_note: the route quantizes activations to DS4 Q8_1 over _MMQ_ACTIVATION_PASSES = 1 plane, the same plane count and the same envelope as the Q4_K gate_up route. Raising the plane count changes a production default's arithmetic and still needs its own gate; that is unchanged and unaddressed here.
executed.not_a_regression_check_that_matters: the model generates degenerate text on this branch -- see the separate finding. Both route settings produce the same degenerate ids, so this change neither caused nor masked it.
